title: Print port monitor DLL registered from a staging or remote path
description: Detects a machine registry DLL registration whose complete value names a DLL in selected profile, temporary, environment-variable or UNC locations.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may register an untrusted print port monitor DLL for execution by the print spooler.
hypothesis.rationale: The registry write does not prove the DLL exists, is malicious or was loaded. Relative DLL names and other locations are outside this deliberately bounded predicate.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Detects a machine registry DLL registration whose complete value names a DLL in selected profile, temporary, environment-variable or UNC locations.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint registry events

triage.summary: The registry write does not prove the DLL exists, is malicious or was loaded. Relative DLL names and other locations are outside this deliberately bounded predicate.
steps: Review the exact registry key, complete DLL path, account and process responsible for the change.
Inspect DLL hash, signature, owner and provenance; check relevant process image-load events and subsequent execution.
Confirm the approved networking, print or compatibility requirement and investigate unexplained persistence changes.
false_positives: Approved print-management products or controlled testing registering a port monitor from a nonstandard path.

validation.expected_outcome: Match the bounded event, key/action/path or successful operation combination; reject one-field mutations, lookalikes and absent required fields. Synthetic tests do not establish live telemetry or production performance.

limitations: The registry write does not prove the DLL exists, is malicious or was loaded. Relative DLL names and other locations are outside this deliberately bounded predicate.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
